newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Italy missing EMU start not serious - Klima.
newsitem.headline: Italy missing EMU start not serious - Klima.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Monday it would not be serious if Italy was not among the founding members of Europe's planned single currency in 1999.

"It is not serious if Italy joins one or two years later," Klima told Austrian state radio. "But of course it is the goal of the Italian government as well as the European Union and Austria that Italy joins the euro-zone as soon as possible."

Italy rejoined the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM), seen as a precusor to European economic and monetary union (EMU), this weekend after it dropped out of the system in 1992 following a wave of currency turmoil.
Klima said he welcomed the lira's return into the ERM, but added the move should not be seen as a sign Italy would automatically join EMU in 1999.
"All finance ministers agree that yesterday's decision was very important but that it was not prejudicial for a decision on who will be in the euro-zone," he said.

"No doubt it would be desirable for Austria if Italy, its second-biggest trading partner, were in the euro-zone from the start. But it is equally important, I would say even more important, that we have a stable euro," Klima added. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
